speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the onset of your right knee swelling and whether you have experienced any joint pain or stiffness, particularly in the morning?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child experienced swelling in other joints, such as the elbows or ankles, or has he had any recent episodes of blood in his urine or stool? I also need to know if he has had any recent fevers, rashes, or prolonged bleeding from minor cuts.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the child have a history of easy bruising or prolonged bleeding from minor cuts, and has he undergone circumcision recently? I would also like to know if there is any family history of hemophilia or other bleeding disorders on either side of the family. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged activated clotting time with a normal prothrombin time strongly suggests a factor VIII or factor IX deficiency, consistent with hemophilia given the family history. To distinguish between Hemophilia A and B, I need specific factor levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII Activity, Factor IX Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX levels are normal, hemophilia is unlikely, so we must consider other causes of hemarthrosis in a young male with a family history. I will request imaging to assess the joint structure and look for signs of other bleeding disorders or inflammatory conditions. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: The parents report no known allergies, normal birth and developmental history for the child.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal factor levels, I need to rule out platelet function disorders or von Willebrand disease. Has the child had any episodes of gum bleeding, nosebleeds, or excessive bleeding after dental work? REQUEST TEST: Platelet Count, Von Willebrand Factor Antigen, and Ristocetin Cofactor Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet count helps rule out thrombocytopenia, but we still need to evaluate for von Willebrand disease or other platelet function defects given the hemarthrosis and family history. Please provide the results for the Von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Ristocetin Cofactor Activity.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, rash, or recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen, Ristocetin Cofactor Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: Since standard coagulation and von Willebrand tests are normal, I need to consider rare clotting factor deficiencies that do not affect PT or aPTT, such as Factor XIII deficiency, which can cause hemarthrosis and has an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. REQUEST TEST: Factor XIII Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: With Factor XIII activity normal and standard coagulation profiles unremarkable, the clinical picture of isolated hemarthrosis in a young male with a family history strongly points towards a deficiency in a contact activation factor, specifically Factor XI deficiency (Hemophilia C), which can present with variable bleeding severity. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia C (Factor XI Deficiency)
